NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, relying critically on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing and HBM suppliers like Micron and SK Hynix for memory, while its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who collectively represent the majority of its explosive data center revenue growth. Its near-monopoly position in AI GPU accelerators gives it exceptional pricing power and strategic leverage over both suppliers and customers, making it a linchpin of the global AI infrastructure buildout.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the center of a vast global supply chain, acting as a capital-light designer that outsources fabrication to world-class partners like TSMC and Samsung while tightly controlling hardware design and software integration. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through carriers, large retailers, and its own stores, while its high-margin Services segment increasingly depends on platform partners like Google and Meta for licensing and ecosystem revenue.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology occupies a critical mid-tier position in the semiconductor supply chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment manufacturers (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research) for its fab operations, with capex running at ~35-40% of revenue. On the downstream side, Micron is increasingly exposed to AI-driven demand through HBM sales to NVIDIA and cloud DRAM/NAND consumption by hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google), while maintaining legacy exposure to mobile and PC markets through Apple and Qualcomm ecosystem relationships.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings sits at the intellectual property layer of the semiconductor industry, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chip designer rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making it uniquely asset-light with upstream dependencies concentrated in EDA software vendors. Its downstream reach is extraordinarily broad — spanning mobile (Apple, Qualcomm), data center (Amazon, NVIDIA), and embedded markets — with royalty revenue tied directly to the volume of ARM-based chips shipped globally.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company positioned in the middle of the data infrastructure supply chain, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and ARM for processor IP, while serving major hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and networking OEMs with custom and merchant silicon solutions. Its strategic pivot toward custom AI accelerators (XPUs) for cloud customers and high-speed data center networking places it at the intersection of the AI infrastructure buildout, making hyperscaler capex cycles a primary demand driver.
